archetype.name: Title Contender (defense-first)
archetype.definition: A team whose margin, not just its record, sits at the top of the league, built on Victor Wembanyama's rim protection, elite rebounding and the league's best ball security, and backed by a 62-win season a year ago.

report.headline: Wembanyama's Spurs are winning on margin, not luck, and might still improve
report.take:
San Antonio is 12-2 and none of it looks borrowed. The Net Rtg of 13 ranks 2nd, with the offense 6th (ORtg 120.1) and the defense 3rd (DRtg 107.1). The W vs Pt Diff is exactly 0: the point differential implies 12 wins and the Spurs have 12. This is a continuation of last season, when they went 62-20, finished 1st on the site and won 13 playoff games. If anything, they have sharpened. DRtg has dropped from 111.3 to 107.1, and the offense is scoring about as well as it did then.

The engine is Wembanyama, and the numbers on him are absurd. He has a BPM of 16.3, an On-Off of 45 and a USG % of 35.1 at a 62.5 TS %, and he is 1st of 92 on the center tab. Around him the formula is unglamorous: the league's lowest TOV % (10.7), a 29 ORB %, a 76.5 DRB % that ranks 2nd, and opponents shooting just 59.5% at the rim (3rd). The offense isn't a shooting show. eFG % sits exactly at the league average and the 3PA Rate ranks 26th. The Spurs win the possession battle and live off the extra shots.

The numbers hide two things that pull in opposite directions. The good one is that the defense is probably better than its 3rd-ranked rating. Opponents are hitting 38.2% from three, 28th in the league, when last year's mark sat at the league average. Little else about this defense suggests that will last. The bad one is that the record leans hard on one man. The frontcourt grades D+ despite having the best center in the league, because the minutes behind him are bleeding: Luke Kornet's On-Off is -36.3 and Carter Bryant's is -34.6. The site has them only 6th of 30, a sign the depth isn't trusted. De'Aaron Fox, whose On-Off is 24.7, is listed out.

The direction is still up. October was 4-2, November is 8-0, and the last five games came with a differential of 19.8 a game. Expect the 70-win pace to cool. Expect this to remain one of the two or three best teams in the league as long as Wembanyama is on the floor.

strengths.title: Wembanyama bends both ends
strengths.body: His BPM of 16.3 and On-Off of 45 dwarf everyone else on the roster, and he is doing it at a 35.1 USG % with a 62.5 TS %. He is the reason opponents shoot so poorly at the rim and the team owns the glass. Volume this efficient at that usage is a talent signal, not a hot streak.

strengths.title: Winning the possession battle
strengths.body: The Spurs turn it over less than anyone (10.7 TOV %), rank 2nd in DRB % and lead the league in rebounds per game. That is how an offense with league-average eFG % still ranks 6th in ORtg. Ball security and rebounding are structural and tend to hold over a season.

strengths.title: A margin with no luck in it
strengths.body: The W vs Pt Diff is 0, and the differential implies all 12 wins. The point differential per game ranks 2nd, so this is not a close-game mirage. Only two of the last ten were decided by single digits late (a one-point win over Dallas and an overtime win at Utah).

concerns.title: The minutes without Wembanyama
concerns.body: The frontcourt grades D+ even with the league's top center, because the bigs behind him are getting run off the floor. Kornet (-36.3), Bryant (-34.6) and Harrison Barnes (-19.4) all carry deep negative On-Off marks. Any absence or foul trouble for Wembanyama exposes a group that hasn't shown it can hold a lead.

concerns.title: Fox out, Castle inefficient
concerns.body: Fox has been the backcourt's most efficient scorer (62.1 TS %) with an On-Off of 24.7, and he is listed out. That pushes more creation onto Stephon Castle, who uses 24.2% of possessions at a 52.8 TS %. The A+ backcourt grade holds largely through Dylan Harper. How long Fox is out isn't in the sheet.

concerns.title: Perimeter leaks, centers scoring
concerns.body: Opponents shoot 38.2% from three, 28th in the league. Opposing centers score 4.4 points over their own averages against San Antonio, 28th by that measure. The three-point number is likely partly noise given the elite rim and eFG % defense. The center scoring is worth watching, since it may reflect Wembanyama roaming as a helper.

trend.note: A 4-2 October gave way to an 8-0 November in which points allowed per game fell to 102.75. The last five came with a 19.8-point differential a game, well above the season's already elite margin.

weekAhead.headline: Three home games and a trip to winless-ish Sacramento
weekAhead.body:
Detroit on Tuesday is the one real test. The Pistons are 8-4, 9th on the site, with a Net Rtg of 5.4 and the 6th-ranked defense. That defense is built to stop guards: it allows the fewest points to shooting guards in the league, exactly where the Spurs' backcourt does its work without Fox. The opening is inside. Detroit's DRB % ranks 23rd, and it gives up a lot to power forwards and plenty of rebounds to centers, which suits Wembanyama and San Antonio's offensive glass.

After that the schedule falls away. The Clippers (4-8) shoot 39.1% from three, 3rd in the league, and that tests San Antonio's one defensive soft spot. They are also 29th in TOV % and 27th at protecting the rim. New Orleans (4-10) has the league's worst DRtg, and Sacramento (1-12, 30th on the site) lets opponents shoot 74.8% at the rim, also worst in the league. Anything short of three wins would be a surprise. Four is the expectation.

keyMatchups.title: Harper and Castle vs Detroit's guards
keyMatchups.body: Detroit allows shooting guards 18.33 points a game, fewest in the league, and its guards are graded A-. With Fox out, Harper (On-Off 29.4) and Castle carry the creation. This is the week's hardest assignment for a backcourt leaning on Castle's 52.8 TS %.

keyMatchups.title: The glass against Detroit
keyMatchups.body: The Pistons rank 23rd in DRB % and allow centers 15.5 rebounds a game. San Antonio's 29 ORB % and league-leading rebounds per game should produce second chances. That is the likeliest way to beat a defense that otherwise holds up.

keyMatchups.title: Clippers' shooting vs Spurs' arc defense
keyMatchups.body: Los Angeles hits 39.1% from three, and San Antonio is allowing 38.2%. If the Spurs' perimeter numbers are real and not noise, a bad team with good shooters is how it shows up. The Clippers' 15.7 TOV % gives the Spurs the possession edge regardless.

weekAhead.watch: How the backcourt scores against Detroit's guard defense without Fox, and whether opponents' three-point shooting finally cools.

restOfSeason.body:
The defense and the possession game are the sustainable parts. Rim protection, defensive rebounding and ball security are habits and personnel, not hot shooting, and they were already there in a 62-win season. Opponents' 38.2% from three should drift back toward the league's 35.2, which would push an already 3rd-ranked defense higher. The offense has room to grow too: its 57.7 TS % trails last season's 59.5. The 70-win pace will cool anyway, because a Net Rtg of 13 is hard to hold over 82 games and a 12-game win streak inflates any early sample. A final record in the 58-65 range, with a Net Rtg settling around 9 to 12, is the reasonable band.

The ceiling and the risk are the same thing: Wembanyama's availability. The gap between his On-Off and the bigs behind him means any extended absence turns a contender into a merely good team. Fox's return matters next most. The backcourt is deep enough to tread water but less efficient without him.

confidence.note: Only 14 games, but the margin, a W vs Pt Diff of 0 and last season's 62 wins all point the same way.
